entries: 5G is the fifth generation of mobile networks. It is much faster than 4G (up to about 10 Gbps), with very low delay, so it suits video, games, self-driving cars and smart cities. India launched 5G on 1 October 2022.
What is the Internet of Things?
The Internet of Things (IoT) is everyday objects connected to the internet: smart bulbs, watches, fans, cameras, farm sensors. They collect data and can be controlled from a phone.
Virtual reality (VR) puts you inside a computer-made 3D world through a headset that tracks your head. It is used for games, training pilots and doctors, and virtual tours.
Augmented reality (AR) adds computer images on top of the real world, through a phone camera or smart glasses. Examples: Snapchat filters, Pokémon GO and placing virtual furniture in your room.

A quantum computer uses qubits, which can be 0 and 1 at the same time (superposition) and linked together (entanglement). For some problems, like simulating molecules or breaking codes, it could be far faster than normal computers. It is still experimental.
An electric vehicle (EV) runs on a battery-powered electric motor instead of petrol or diesel. It has no exhaust smoke, is cheaper to run and quieter. You charge it at home or at charging stations.
A drone is an aircraft with no pilot on board, flown by remote control or by computer. Drones are used for photography, farming (spraying crops), deliveries, mapping and rescue.
Robotics is the science of designing and building robots: machines that sense their surroundings, decide and act. Robots work in factories, hospitals, space, homes (robot vacuums) and warehouses.
A chatbot is a computer program that talks with people in text or voice. Simple ones follow rules; advanced ones use AI language models to understand and answer questions. MK.ai is a chatbot!
Generative AI creates new content (text, pictures, music, video or code) from what it learned from examples. Chatbots, image makers and video makers are generative AI.
A deepfake is a fake video, photo or voice made with AI to look and sound like a real person. They can spread lies, so check sources before believing or sharing shocking clips.
An NFT (non-fungible token) is a unique digital certificate on a blockchain that shows who owns a digital item, like a picture or game item.
A smartwatch is a wrist computer that shows time, messages and calls, and tracks steps, heart rate, sleep and workouts. It usually pairs with your phone.
A 3D printer builds an object layer by layer from a computer design, usually with melted plastic. It is used for models, spare parts, medical implants and even houses.
Edge computing processes data close to where it is made (in a phone, camera or local server) instead of far-away cloud data centres, so responses are faster.
A data centre is a building full of computers (servers) that store data and run websites, apps and cloud services. They need lots of power and cooling.
DigiLocker is the Indian government's free app for keeping official documents digitally: Aadhaar, driving licence, marksheets and more. Digital copies from it are legally valid.
Aadhaar is a 12-digit identity number for residents of India, linked to fingerprints, iris scans and a photo. It is issued by UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) and was started in 2009.
Digital India is a government programme, launched on 1 July 2015, to bring internet, online services and digital skills to every Indian. UPI, DigiLocker, Aadhaar and BharatNet are part of it.
ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) is an Indian government network that lets buyers and sellers on different apps trade with each other, so small shops can sell online too.
FASTag is a sticker on a vehicle's windscreen with an RFID chip that pays highway tolls automatically from a linked account, so cars don't stop at toll plazas.
RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) uses radio waves to read a small chip or tag without touching it. It is used in FASTag, library books, shop security tags and ID cards.
NFC (Near Field Communication) lets two devices share data when held a few centimetres apart. It powers tap-to-pay cards and phone payments.
Bluetooth is short-range wireless technology (about 10 metres) for connecting earphones, speakers, watches and phones. It is named after King Harald Bluetooth of Denmark.
